prerequisites: Skills developed in the courses 'Mathematical Analysis 1' and 'Linear Algebra and Elements of Geometry'

learning_outcomes.text: Know and be able to apply numerical methods for root finding, interpolation, and numerical integration.
Understand and use numerical methods for solving ordinary differential equations.
Acquire basic notions of numerical optimization, with particular reference to gradient-based methods.
Develop a critical approach in the selection, application, and evaluation of numerical methods.
Refine mathematical language and the ability to formulate and solve problems rigorously.
Understand and be able to discuss the main methods of analysis of numerical series and know the basics of function series.
Master theoretical solution techniques for ordinary differential equations.

syllabus_topics: Numerical methods for root finding, including the bisection method, fixed-point iteration, Newton's method.
Introduction to numerical integration, including the rectangle, trapezoidal, and Cavalieri-Simpson rules.
One-step numerical methods for ordinary differential equations, with particular emphasis on the forward Euler method.
Introduction to optimization, including unconstrained optimization by gradient descent methods and constrained optimization by the method of Lagrange multipliers.
Series: numerical series and related classical intuitions, convergence, series with positive terms, series with variable sign terms, basics of function series with applications.
Ordinary differential equations: basic notions, first-order equations, second-order linear equations.

Functions of several variables: elementary properties of R^n, limits and continuity, partial derivatives, gradient, tangent plane, differentiability and directional derivatives, higher-order derivatives and Hessian matrix, Taylor polynomials, basics of partial differential equations with applications, double integrals.

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (compulsory for a grade higher than 27)

assessment_rules: Assessment includes a compulsory written exam and two partial/in-progress exams. An oral exam is required to obtain a final grade higher than 27/30. The maximum grade without an oral exam is 27/30. Grades above 27/30 and 'cum laude' require the oral exam, demonstrating critical analysis and mastery of the subject.
bibliography: M. Bertsch, R. Dal Passo e L. Giacomelli, Analisi matematica, McGraw-Hill.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Biomedica (Biomedical Engineering), classe L-9 R Ingegneria industriale
